section: Section Four — The Tosefta, Talmud, and Geonim
subtitle: R. Chiyya's Tosefta, the Babylonian Talmud, the Geonim, and the Alfasi
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's general introduction to his Commentary on the Mishnah — tracing the oral tradition from Sinai through the Zugot, Rebbi's compilation of the Mishnah, the Talmud and Geonim, and his own methodology. Original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic with English translation.

aligned.en: R. Chiyya now sought to compose a work in which he would follow the traces of his teacher and clarify whatever was difficult in his teacher's words — this is the Tosefta. His purpose in it was to elucidate the Mishnah and to add cases that can be derived from the Mishnah, though only after considerable effort; he derived them so as to teach us how we too should derive and draw conclusions from the Mishnah.

aligned.en: Now everyone who arose after him and after that illustrious assembly had as his sole aim to grasp the words of the Mishnah; generation after generation continued to study it and expound it, each scholar according to the measure of his learning and understanding. aligned.en: Rav Ashi devoted himself to compilation, and saw fit to do with the words of all who came after our holy master what our holy master had done with the words of all who came after Moses. So he gathered all the statements of those who had spoken, the analyses of those who had analyzed, and the interpretations of the interpreters; he verified the traditions and collected them, and grasped the whole in his learning by virtue of the breadth of soul and the love of knowledge God had granted him. Thus he compiled the Talmud, and made his purpose in it fourfold.

aligned.en: The first is the interpretation of the Mishnah and of all that occurs in its ambiguous language by way of differing interpretations, the arguments each interpreter brings against his fellow, and the demonstration of which view is the truth — this is the first of his purposes. The second is the rendering of a decisive ruling in accordance with the view of one of the disputing parties whose disagreement arose over the text of the Mishnah, or over its interpretation, or over what is derived and inferred from it.

aligned.en: This fourth purpose — I mean the homily occurring in the Talmud — should not be supposed to be of low rank or of little benefit; on the contrary, it is of immense value, for the strange riddles and wondrous insights it comprises. For when you examine these *derashot* with an inner gaze, you grasp from them the most absolute good, beyond which there is no surpassing; there is disclosed in them divine meanings and the true realities of all that the people of knowledge speculate about and all that the philosophers across the ages have determined.

One of these is to sharpen the minds of students; another is to blind those fools whose hearts have never been illumined — for were the truths laid plainly before them, they would turn away from them in proportion to the deficiency of their natures.

aligned.en: They saw that every artificial existent has a known end requiring no inquiry, since its maker does not make it unless its end is already conceived in his mind. Likewise the end of the adze is to plane with it, and the needle to join cloth to cloth with it; and so for all things brought into being through artifice.

בידה, ואלכ'יל ליקטע בהא מסאפה טוילה פי
זמאן יסיר. ומנהא אנואע לא נערף להא מנפעה
ופיהא מנאפע לאלאנסאן לא יעלם בהא.

pairs.en: Mishnah and the construal of its wording.

aligned.ja:
לאנך לו סאלת אכבר גאון ען תפסיר
הלכה מן אלמשנה לם יסתטע אן יקול לך פיהא
שיא אלא אן כאן יחפט' תלמוד תלך אלהלכה,
או יקול אלי אן ננט'ר מא וקע פיהא מן
אלכלאם פי אלתלמוד, ולא פי אסתטאעהֵ שכ'ץ
אן יכון יחפט' ג'מלהֵ אלתלמוד, ולא סימא
בכון אלהלכה אלואחדה מן אלמשנה קד תתפסר
פי ארבע אוראק וכ'מס, לאן ידכ'ל כלאם עלי
כלאם, ואלחג'ג' ואלאעתראצ'את ואלאג'ובה,
חתי לא יקדר אן ילכ'ץ מא צפי פי תאויל תלך
אלמשנה אלא מאהר פי אלנט'ר.
aligned.en: For if you asked the greatest Gaon for the interpretation of a *halakhah* of the Mishnah, he would not be able to tell you anything about it unless he had the Talmud of that *halakhah* by heart, or he would say, "Wait until we look at what is said about it in the Talmud" — and it is not within the power of any person to have the whole of the Talmud by heart, especially since a single *halakhah* of the Mishnah is sometimes interpreted over four or five pages, because discourse enters upon discourse, with arguments, objections, and answers, so that no one can extract what is pure in the construal of that Mishnah unless he is a master of inquiry.

אלד'י ארומה. וקצדנא פי הד'א אלתאליף תפסיר
אלמשנה בחסב מא פסר אלתלמוד, ואלאקתצאר
עלי אלתפאסיר אלצחיחה, ואכ'תצאר אלתפאסיר
אלתי ט'הר בטלאנהא פי אלתלמוד, ואט'האר
אלעלל אלתי לאג'להא אתצ'ע ד'לך אלכלאם,
ואלעלל אלתי לאג'להא וקע אלאכ'תלאף בין
אלמכ'תלפין פי בעץ' אלאכ'תלאפאת, ועלי מד'הב
מן אלעמל עלי מא יבין אלתלמוד.
aligned.en: When these meanings had taken shape for me, I devoted myself to the compilation I aim at. Our intent in this compilation is to interpret the Mishnah according to how the Talmud interpreted it, to confine ourselves to the sound interpretations, to abridge the interpretations whose falsity is shown in the Talmud, to exhibit the reasons for which a given statement became clear, the reasons for which disagreement arose among the disputants in some of the disagreements, and which view is to be acted upon according to what the Talmud makes clear.
